messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up to the RFC — proposing we decouple RBAC evaluation from tile materialization in the console query path. Right now our flow is auth -> materialize -> render and when the permissions tables grow p95 spikes. Idea: apply a cheap, coarse prefilter before heavy materialization and keep a full per-item evaluation as a fallback/audit step. Who sees major gotchas?

Rahul: Short: this should cut materialization work and p95, but adds read amplification (extra index/lookup) and more cache surface. Worth it but need numbers.

Liz: Main worry is staleness. If we prefilter by cached perms we need fast invalidation when roles change. Otherwise we'll either overblock or worse, leak.

Kevin: We can mitigate with versioned permission keys. Add permission_version to the cache key so role updates bump the version and invalidate automatically.

Maya: Also thought about a two-tier filter: 1) tenant-level coarse mask (cheap, low FP), 2) optional probabilistic membership (bloom) for fine-grained prefilter. If bloom says 'no' we drop early; if 'yes' run final eval.

Rahul: Careful — bloom false positives are fine (they just pass to final eval) but false positives could cause more materialization, and false negatives would drop valid rows. Bloom typically has false positives, not negatives, so we wouldn't accidentally drop valid data. But we must never rely on bloom to allow access without final eval.

Liz: We must avoid any path that could return sensitive fields before final eval. So design rule: prefilter only reduces candidate set; final per-item evaluation must always gate the actual response. That keeps safety but may reduce perf benefits if many items survive to final eval.

Kevin: Operational thought: run a simulation: current baseline median seq=40, proposed prefilter removes ~60% of rows based on telemetry => materialization ops drop proportionally. Rough calc: 10k qps -> ~30% CPU/GPU saving. We'll need an A/B loadtest.

Maya: Proposed rollout plan: (1) implement coarse prefilter behind feature flag (tenant_mask + role_mask), (2) add tracing spans for 'rbac_prefilter' and 'rbac_final_eval', (3) canary on subset of tenants, measure materialized_rows, post_filter_count, and e2e p95. If >40% materialization reduction with no auth regressions, widen rollout.

Liz: Metrics to add to console telemetry: materialized_rows, candidates_after_prefilter, final_authorized_count, rbac_invalidation_events, rbac_stale_errors. Also add alert if (candidates_after_prefilter / materialized_rows) > 0.9 for 5m (meaning prefilter useless).

Devon: deploy-bot: Canary deploy window requested: 2025-06-10T20:00Z -> cluster-console-canary. Will create rollout ticket.

Maya: Example config sketch (will be in PR):
```
rbac_prefilter:
  type: tenant_mask
  ttl_seconds: 60
  allow_fallback_to_full_eval: true
```

Rahul: Also: consider invalidation bus integration (KVS pub/sub) so control-plane role updates push invalidations to edge caches. Without that TTLs will either cause staleness or high churn.

Liz: Agreed. Integrate with existing policy-change webhook. Also add a regression test that flips a role and asserts immediate deny/allow semantics for canary tenants.

Maya: Sounds like consensus. I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with interface + telemetry + canary plan. Sync tomorrow morning 10:30 to review impl choices. :thumbsup:

Rahul: SGTM.

Kevin: Thanks — excited to see the numbers.

Devon: deploy-bot: Noted, ticket created: CONSOLE-1921.
